papers.title: Crime on ICE: Local Police Behavior and Immigration Enforcement in the United States
papers.abstract: A growing number of local police departments now hold authority to enforce federal immigration law, a role traditionally reserved for federal officers. Despite claims that this authority enhances public safety, empirical evidence remains limited. Using FBI Uniform Crime Report data from 2000–2024, we exploit staggered adoption across U.S. jurisdictions to estimate causal effects on policing. We find that this enforcement authority increases arrests for low-level, discretionary offenses by approximately 7%, with no corresponding decreases in offense rates or serious crime. These results suggest that such agreements realign police priorities toward discretionary enforcement without measurable public safety benefits.

papers.title: Measuring the Impact of Impact Measurement
papers.abstract: Impact measurement is central to impact investing and social entrepreneurship, yet little is known about whether firms benefit privately from measuring impact. We conduct the first randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms exhibit nearly twice as much revenue growth and raise nearly twice as much capital as control firms. In a companion experiment with early-stage investors, we find that investors respond strongly to quantified impact metrics but not to generic qualitative impact statements. Together, our results show that impact measurement can shape firm growth and capital allocation.
